 Corona secured Mexico’s berth at CNL Finals and 2027 Gold Cup 
 11/18/2026 - 6:04 AM share-facebook share-x share-whatsapp share-copy-link Mexico Clinches CNL Finals Berth El Tricolor also qualified for the 2027 Gold Cup. 
 GUADALUPE, Nuevo Leon – League A action in the 2026/27 Concacaf Nations League continued on Tuesday, with Mexico securing a place in the 2027 Concacaf Nations League Finals and the 2027 Concacaf Gold Cup after a 1-nil win over Jamaica , advancing on the away goals rule after the series finished 3-3 on aggregate at Estadio BBVA in Guadalupe, Nuevo Leon, Mexico.
 After several early attempts to open the scoring and level the aggregate score, Mexico broke through in the 35’ thanks to a left-footed strike from the edge of the box by Jesús Corona , following a pass from Julián Quiñones .
 View this post on Instagram 
 Roberto Alvarado tried to double Mexico’s lead before the half time whistle, however, Jamaican goalkeeper Jahmali Waite made an important save that kept the score at the break.
 Both teams went all the way to get the ball to the back of the net in the second half, however, the defensive backlines made it impossible for both attacking lines to find a space to score, Corona’s goal becoming the only one of the night.
 This marks the first win for newly appointed Mexican Head Coach Rafael Márquez , as he began his career ahead of El Tricolor with two draws and three defeats, including the 2026/2027 CNL Quarterfinals First Leg.
 With this result, the Quarterfinals series ended in a 3-3 aggregate score, with Mexico securing their spot in the 2026/2027 Concacaf Nations League Finals due to away goals difference. The North Americans also booked their ticket to the 2027 Gold Cup.
 Post-Match Data: Mexico vs. Jamaica
 Mexico's Julián Quiñones has recorded more goal contributions in his last two Concacaf Nations League appearances (2: one goal and one assist) than in his previous five matches combined in the competition (one goal).
 Jamaica's Kyle Ming won more tackles (3) than any other player on the field, despite being substituted in the 62nd minute. Teammates Richard King and Ronaldo Webster, along with Mexico's Mateo Chávez and Álvaro Fidalgo, were tied for second with two successful tackles each.
 Mexico did not allow Jamaica a single shot on target, marking the first time El Tri has held an opponent without a shot on target in a Concacaf Nations League match.
 Israel Reyes completed 92 passes against Jamaica, the most by a Mexican player in a single Concacaf Nations League match in the competition's history. He also recorded a 93% passing accuracy rate, completing 92 of his 99 attempted passes.
 Mexico is one of only two nations to have participated in every edition of the Concacaf Nations League. El Tri is also the only team to have finished among the top three in every previous edition, finishing third in 2021 and 2024, and second in 2023.
